title: 1 Kings 13 — The man of the Elohim from Yehudah and the torn altar at Beit-El (Bethel)

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ אִ֣ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֗ים בָּ֧א מִיהוּדָ֛ה בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וְיָרָבְעָ֛ם עֹמֵ֥ד עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לְהַקְטִֽיר׃

i18n.en: And behold, a man of Elohim came out of Yehudah by the word of YHWH to Beit-El; and Yarov'am was standing by the altar to burn incense.

notes.official:
*wəhinnēh ʾîš ʾĕlōhîm bāʾ mîhûḏâ biḏḇar YHWH* 'And behold, a man of Elohim came out of Yehudah by the word of YHWH'. The title is anarthrous here and articular at its fourteen later occurrences (vv 4-31), where the article marks the man already introduced. The translation follows the Hebrew article in both forms, 'a man of Elohim' / 'the man of the Elohim', as at 17:18, 24 and 2 Kgs 1:9-13 (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`). Grammatically the article on the genitive makes the whole construct chain definite (GKC §127a; Joüon-Muraoka §139a), so 'the man of Elohim' would be an acceptable English alternative; the convention keeps the Hebrew form visible across Kings. ASV and the English edition of *The Book Which Tells the Truth*: 'a man of God'.

*biḏḇar YHWH* 'by the word of YHWH' occurs seven times in the chapter (vv 1, 2, 5, 9, 17, 18, 32), which turns on the authority of that word. Names: Yehudah = Judah; Beit-El = Bethel (central `bethel-luz-name-etymology`); Yarov'am = Jeroboam. *ʿōmēḏ ʿal-hammizbēaḥ ləhaqṭîr* 'standing by the altar to burn incense': *ʿal* can also mean 'on', i.e. on the altar platform.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 1-5; see the note at v 5.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מִזְבֵּ֣חַ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּֽה־בֵ֞ן נוֹלָ֤ד לְבֵית־דָּוִד֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ שְׁמ֔וֹ וְזָבַ֣ח עָלֶ֗יךָ אֶת־כֹּהֲנֵ֤י הַבָּמוֹת֙ הַמַּקְטִרִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יךָ וְעַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָ֖ם יִשְׂרְפ֥וּ עָלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And he cried against the altar by the word of YHWH, and said, "O altar, altar, thus says YHWH: 'Behold, a son shall be born to the house of David, Yoshiyahu by name; and upon you he shall sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense upon you, and human bones shall they burn upon you.'"

notes.official:
*mizbēaḥ mizbēaḥ* 'O altar, altar': the oracle is addressed to the altar itself. Yoshiyahu = Josiah; the fulfilment is narrated at 2 Kgs 23:15-20, which refers back to this prophecy. Critical scholarship generally reads the naming of a king three centuries later as written in the light of that fulfilment (Noth; Cogan, *1 Kings*, AB 10), and traditional exegesis reads it as prediction; the translation renders the text as it stands.

*kōhănê habbāmôṯ* 'the priests of the high places' (ASV): *bāmâ* is a raised cultic platform or local shrine (BDB; Vaughan, *The Meaning of 'bāmâ' in the Old Testament*, 1974). 'High places' is kept here, at vv 32-33 and at 22:44 as the established English term. *ʿaṣmôṯ ʾāḏām* 'human bones' (central `adam-adamah`, 'the human').

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַן֩ בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֤וּא מוֹפֵת֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֣ה הַמּוֹפֵ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֤ה הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ נִקְרָ֔ע וְנִשְׁפַּ֖ךְ הַדֶּ֥שֶׁן אֲשֶׁר־עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he gave a sign the same day, saying, "This is the sign which YHWH has spoken: 'Behold, the altar shall be torn, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.'"

notes.official:
*wənāṯan ... môp̄ēṯ* 'And he gave a sign' (ASV): *môp̄ēṯ* is a portent or wonder that authenticates a word (Ex 7:9; Deut 13:2-3); here it is announced and fulfilled the same day (v 5). 'Sign' is kept.

*hinnēh hammizbēaḥ niqrāʿ* 'Behold, the altar shall be torn' (ASV 'rent', which the English edition of *The Book Which Tells the Truth* quotes; French edition 'va se fendre'). The Niphal of *qrʿ* 'tear, rend' is normally used of cloth. It is the keyword of the Yarov'am narrative, in which YHWH 'tears' the kingdom from Shelomoh's house (11:11-13, 30-31; 14:8), and 'torn' keeps that link (`niqra-ha-mizbeach-the-altar-torn-1-kings-13`). *wənišpaḵ haddešen* 'and the ashes ... shall be poured out': *dešen* is the fat-soaked ash of the sacrifices, whose proper disposal is prescribed at Lev 4:12 (*šep̄eḵ haddešen*); spilled on the spot, it leaves the altar unfit.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָרָ֤א עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֔ל וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יָרָבְעָ֧ם אֶת־יָד֛וֹ מֵעַ֥ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לֵאמֹ֣ר ׀ תִּפְשֻׂ֑הוּ וַתִּיבַ֤שׁ יָדוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֣ח עָלָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לַהֲשִׁיבָ֥הּ אֵלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when the king heard the word of the man of the Elohim which he cried against the altar in Beit-El, that Yarov'am stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him." And his hand, which he stretched out against him, dried up, so that he could not draw it back to himself.

notes.official:
*wattîḇaš yāḏô* 'And his hand ... dried up' (ASV; *The Book Which Tells the Truth*, English edition 'dried up', French 'se dessécha'): *yāḇēš* 'be dry, wither' is used of a withered or paralysed limb (Zech 11:17). 'Dried up' is kept as the literal rendering; NRSV 'withered' and NJPS 'became rigid' interpret the effect. *wəlōʾ yāḵōl lahăšîḇāh ʾēlāyw* 'so that he could not draw it back to himself'. The king stretches out his hand 'from the altar' (*mēʿal hammizbēaḥ*), i.e. from his place at it (v 1). Articular title 'the man of the Elohim' (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) reads the episode as one of the creators burning the king's hand and destroying the altar with an 'atomic disintegrator'. The line renders *wattîḇaš* lexically ('dried up'); the Hebrew names neither a burn nor a device.

paragraphs.text: וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ נִקְרָ֔ע וַיִּשָּׁפֵ֥ךְ הַדֶּ֖שֶׁן מִן־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כַּמּוֹפֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛ן אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: The altar also was torn, and the ashes were poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of the Elohim had given by the word of YHWH.

notes.official:
*wəhammizbēaḥ niqrāʿ* 'The altar also was torn' (v 3; `niqra-ha-mizbeach-the-altar-torn-1-kings-13`). *kammôp̄ēṯ ʾăšer nāṯan ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm* 'according to the sign which the man of the Elohim had given'. The fulfilment comes at once, before the king's hand is restored (v 6).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 1-5 ('the altar shall be rent ... the altar also was rent') and reads them as the destruction of the altar by one of the creators by means of an 'atomic disintegrator'. The line renders the Niphal of *qrʿ* as the major versions do ('rent', 'torn', 'broken apart') and does not encode a mechanism.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֨עַן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ אֶל־אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים חַל־נָ֞א אֶת־פְּנֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ וְהִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲדִ֔י וְתָשֹׁ֥ב יָדִ֖י אֵלָ֑י וַיְחַ֤ל אִישׁ־הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַתָּ֤שָׁב יַד־הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַתְּהִ֖י כְּבָרִֽאשֹׁנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the king answered and said to the man of the Elohim, "Entreat now the favor of YHWH your Elohim, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me." And the man of the Elohim entreated YHWH, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before.

notes.official: *ḥal-nāʾ ʾeṯ-pənê YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā* 'Entreat now the favor of YHWH your Elohim' (ASV), literally 'soften the face of YHWH', the idiom of appeasing a superior (Ex 32:11; 1 Sam 13:12; Zech 7:2). The second occurrence, *wayəḥal ... ʾeṯ-pənê YHWH*, is rendered 'entreated YHWH' with the ASV; the literal phrase is recorded here. *wəhiṯpallēl baʿăḏî* 'and pray for me': intercession is a prophetic function (central `navi-first-occurrence-abraham`, Gen 20:7, cites this verse). The title occurs twice in the verse, both articular.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים בֹּאָה־אִתִּ֥י הַבַּ֖יְתָה וּֽסְעָ֑דָה וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לְךָ֖ מַתָּֽת׃

i18n.en: And the king said to the man of the Elohim, "Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward."

notes.official: *ûsəʿāḏâ* 'and refresh yourself' (*sʿd* 'sustain', with food). *mattāṯ* 'a reward' (ASV), a gift.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אִישׁ־הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־תִּתֶּן־לִי֙ אֶת־חֲצִ֣י בֵיתֶ֔ךָ לֹ֥א אָבֹ֖א עִמָּ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־אֹ֤כַל לֶ֙חֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶשְׁתֶּה־מַּ֔יִם בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And the man of the Elohim said to the king, "If you give me half your house, I will not go in with you, nor will I eat bread nor drink water in this place;

notes.official: *ʾim-tittēn-lî ʾeṯ-ḥăṣî ḇêṯeḵā* 'If you give me half your house': an emphatic refusal. Commentators read the ban on eating and drinking 'in this place' as a refusal of any communion with the Beit-El sanctuary (Gray, *I & II Kings*, OTL; Cogan); it sets up the test of vv 15-22.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־כֵ֣ן ׀ צִוָּ֣ה אֹתִ֗י בִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹא־תֹ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁתֶּה־מָּ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א תָשׁ֔וּב בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽכְתָּ׃

i18n.en: for so was I commanded by the word of YHWH, saying, 'You shall eat no bread, nor drink water, nor return by the way that you went.'"

notes.official:
*wəlōʾ ṯāšûḇ baddereḵ ʾăšer hālāḵtā* 'nor return by the way that you went': the third prohibition. *dereḵ* 'way' is a keyword of the chapter (vv 9, 10, 12, 17, 24-28, 33).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 9-10 and reads the instruction as a measure to keep the route back to a terrestrial camp of the Elohim from being discovered. The line renders the prohibition as the Hebrew gives it; the text itself gives no reason for it.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אַחֵ֑ר וְלֹֽא־שָׁ֣ב בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֛ר בָּ֥א בָ֖הּ אֶל־בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So he went another way, and did not return by the way that he came to Beit-El.

notes.official: *wayyēleḵ bədereḵ ʾaḥēr* 'So he went another way': the narrator records obedience to the third command (see the reception note at v 9). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) follows.

paragraphs.text: וְנָבִ֤יא אֶחָד֙ זָקֵ֔ן יֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֑ל וַיָּב֣וֹא בְנ֡וֹ וַיְסַפֶּר־ל֣וֹ אֶת־כָּל־הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂה֩ אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֨ים ׀ הַיּ֜וֹם בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֗ל אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיְסַפְּר֖וּם לַאֲבִיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Now there dwelt an old prophet in Beit-El; and his son came and told him all the deeds that the man of the Elohim had done that day in Beit-El; the words which he had spoken to the king, these they told to their father.

notes.official: *wənāḇîʾ ʾeḥāḏ zāqēn* 'an old prophet' (central `navi-first-occurrence-abraham`). MT *wayyāḇôʾ ḇənô* 'and his son came' is singular, followed by plural verbs ('these they told'). The LXX, Syriac and Vulgate read 'his sons', and the ASV harmonizes with 'one of his sons'. The MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`); a shift from singular to plural when others join in is common in Hebrew narrative.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אֲבִיהֶ֔ם אֵֽי־זֶ֥ה הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ הָלָ֑ךְ וַיִּרְא֣וּ בָנָ֗יו אֶת־הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלַךְ֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖א מִיהוּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: And their father said to them, "Which way did he go?" And his sons had seen the way which the man of the Elohim went, who came from Yehudah.

notes.official: MT *wayyirʾû ḇānāyw ʾeṯ-haddereḵ* 'And his sons had seen the way' (Qal; ASV likewise). The LXX, Syriac, Targum and Vulgate presuppose the Hiphil *wayyarʾuhû* 'and his sons showed him the way', which differs by one consonant and the vowels. The MT is construable and is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־בָּנָ֔יו חִבְשׁוּ־לִ֖י הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַיַּחְבְּשׁוּ־ל֣וֹ הַחֲמ֔וֹר וַיִּרְכַּ֖ב עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode on it.

notes.official: *ḥiḇšû-lî haḥămôr* 'Saddle the donkey for me' (ASV 'ass'). The donkey recurs in vv 23-29; standing unharmed beside the lion, it marks the death as no ordinary attack (v 28).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּ֨מְצָאֵ֔הוּ יֹשֵׁ֖ב תַּ֣חַת הָאֵלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו הַאַתָּ֧ה אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אתָ מִֽיהוּדָ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אָֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And he went after the man of the Elohim and found him sitting under the oak; and he said to him, "Are you the man of the Elohim who came from Yehudah?" And he said, "I am."

notes.official: *taḥaṯ hāʾēlâ* 'under the oak' (ASV): *ʾēlâ* is usually the terebinth, a landmark tree. The central `eshel-tamarisk-cultic-site` entry cites this verse for the sacred-tree vocabulary but governs *ʾešel* only. *haʾattâ ʾîš-hāʾĕlōhîm* 'Are you the man of the Elohim ...?' (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו לֵ֥ךְ אִתִּ֖י הַבָּ֑יְתָה וֶאֱכֹ֖ל לָֽחֶם׃

i18n.en: Then he said to him, "Come home with me and eat bread."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֥א אוּכַ֛ל לָשׁ֥וּב אִתָּ֖ךְ וְלָב֣וֹא אִתָּ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־אֹ֣כַל לֶ֗חֶם וְלֹֽא־אֶשְׁתֶּ֤ה אִתְּךָ֙ מַ֔יִם בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And he said, "I may not return with you, nor go in with you; neither will I eat bread nor drink water with you in this place;

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־דָבָ֤ר אֵלַי֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לֹֽא־תֹאכַ֣ל לֶ֔חֶם וְלֹֽא־תִשְׁתֶּ֥ה שָׁ֖ם מָ֑יִם לֹא־תָשׁ֣וּב לָלֶ֔כֶת בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־הָלַ֥כְתָּ בָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: for a word came to me by the word of YHWH, 'You shall eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn back to go by the way that you went.'"

notes.official: *kî-ḏāḇār ʾēlay biḏḇar YHWH* 'for a word came to me by the word of YHWH': the doubled *dāḇār* stresses the source of the command.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ גַּם־אֲנִ֣י נָבִיא֮ כָּמוֹךָ֒ וּמַלְאָ֡ךְ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלַי֩ בִּדְבַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲשִׁבֵ֤הוּ אִתְּךָ֙ אֶל־בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ וְיֹ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְיֵ֣שְׁתְּ מָ֑יִם כִּחֵ֖שׁ לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he said to him, "I also am a prophet as you are; and a messenger spoke to me by the word of YHWH, saying, 'Bring him back with you into your house, that he may eat bread and drink water.'" He lied to him.

notes.official: *gam-ʾănî nāḇîʾ kāmôḵā* 'I also am a prophet as you are'. *ûmalʾāḵ dibber ʾēlay* 'and a messenger spoke to me' (ASV 'an angel'): *malʾāḵ* is 'messenger' throughout the corpus (central `malakh-yhwh-messenger`; cf. 1 Kgs 19:5). The old prophet claims a heavenly messenger speaking *biḏḇar YHWH*, a source the man of the Elohim cannot check. *kiḥēš lô* 'He lied to him': a two-word comment by the narrator; no motive is given.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣שָׁב אִתּ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֛חֶם בְּבֵית֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥שְׁתְּ מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: So he went back with him, and ate bread in his house, and drank water.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֕י הֵ֥ם יֹשְׁבִ֖ים אֶל־הַשֻּׁלְחָ֑ן (פ) וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֱשִׁיבֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of YHWH came to the prophet who had brought him back;

notes.official: *wayəhî dəḇar-YHWH ʾel-hannāḇîʾ* 'that the word of YHWH came to the prophet who had brought him back' (central `davar-yhwh-prophetic-formula`): the true word now comes through the prophet who lied. The MT has a section mark (פ) in the middle of the verse, after 'as they sat at the table' (*pisqāʾ bəʾemṣaʿ pāsûq*; central `piska-b-emtza-pasuq-masoretic-paragraph-break`). The Hebrew text keeps the mark; the English runs on without a break, as the ASV does, and as at 2 Kgs 1:17.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֞א אֶל־אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤א מִֽיהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה יַ֗עַן כִּ֤י מָרִ֙יתָ֙ פִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֙רְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: and he cried to the man of the Elohim who came from Yehudah, saying, "Thus says YHWH: 'Because you have disobeyed the mouth of YHWH, and have not kept the commandment which YHWH your Elohim commanded you,

notes.official: *yaʿan kî mārîṯā pî YHWH* 'Because you have disobeyed the mouth of YHWH' (ASV 'been disobedient unto the mouth'): *mrh* is 'be rebellious, defy', and *pî YHWH* 'the mouth of YHWH' is his spoken command (also v 26; Num 20:24; Deut 1:26). 'Disobeyed' is kept as the ASV sense; 'rebelled against' is the stronger literal rendering.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּ֗שָׁב וַתֹּ֤אכַל לֶ֙חֶם֙ וַתֵּ֣שְׁתְּ מַ֔יִם בַּמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־תֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְאַל־תֵּ֣שְׁתְּ מָ֑יִם לֹֽא־תָב֥וֹא נִבְלָתְךָ֖ אֶל־קֶ֥בֶר אֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: but came back, and have eaten bread and drunk water in the place of which he said to you, "Eat no bread and drink no water"; your body shall not come to the grave of your fathers.'"

notes.official: *lōʾ-ṯāḇôʾ niḇlāṯəḵā ʾel-qeḇer ʾăḇōṯeyḵā* 'your body shall not come to the grave of your fathers' (ASV 'body'). *nəḇēlâ* (vv 22, 24, 25, 28, 29, 30) is a corpse or carcass, often one left exposed (Deut 21:23; Jer 7:33); some modern versions render 'corpse'. 'Body' is kept with the ASV, and the stronger sense is recorded here. Burial away from the family tomb was a curse (cf. 14:11).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵ֛י אָכְל֥וֹ לֶ֖חֶם וְאַחֲרֵ֣י שְׁתוֹת֑וֹ וַיַּחֲבָשׁ־ל֣וֹ הַחֲמ֔וֹר לַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֱשִׁיבֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for him, for the prophet whom he had brought back.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ וַיִּמְצָאֵ֧הוּ אַרְיֵ֛ה בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ וַתְּהִ֤י נִבְלָתוֹ֙ מֻשְׁלֶ֣כֶת בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהַחֲמוֹר֙ עֹמֵ֣ד אֶצְלָ֔הּ וְהָ֣אַרְיֵ֔ה עֹמֵ֖ד אֵ֥צֶל הַנְּבֵלָֽה׃

i18n.en: And he went, and a lion met him on the way and killed him; and his body was thrown in the way, and the donkey stood beside it; the lion also stood beside the body.

notes.official: *wayyimṣāʾēhû ʾaryēh* 'and a lion met him' (ASV; literally 'found him'). *wattəhî niḇlāṯô mušleḵeṯ baddereḵ* 'and his body was thrown in the way'. The lion stands beside the body without eating it, and the donkey is unharmed (v 28): the narrative marks the death as a judgement, not a natural attack.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֣ים עֹבְרִ֗ים וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֶת־הַנְּבֵלָה֙ מֻשְׁלֶ֣כֶת בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְאֶת־הָ֣אַרְיֵ֔ה עֹמֵ֖ד אֵ֣צֶל הַנְּבֵלָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ בָעִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֛ר הַנָּבִ֥יא הַזָּקֵ֖ן יֹשֵׁ֥ב בָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And behold, men passed by and saw the body thrown in the way, and the lion standing beside the body; and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע הַנָּבִיא֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֱשִׁיב֣וֹ מִן־הַדֶּרֶךְ֒ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֣ים ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָרָ֖ה אֶת־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֨הוּ יְהוָ֜ה לָאַרְיֵ֗ה וַֽיִּשְׁבְּרֵ֙הוּ֙ וַיְמִתֵ֔הוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּר־לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And when the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard of it, he said, "It is the man of the Elohim, who disobeyed the mouth of YHWH; therefore YHWH has given him to the lion, which has mauled him and killed him, according to the word of YHWH which he spoke to him."

notes.official: *wayyittənēhû YHWH lāʾaryēh wayyišbərēhû wayəmiṯēhû* 'therefore YHWH has given him to the lion, which has mauled him and killed him' (ASV 'torn'). *šbr* is 'break', used of a beast mangling its prey (BDB *šāḇar*; HALOT). 'Torn' would give one English word to two Hebrew verbs in the same chapter, *qrʿ* at vv 3, 5 and *šbr* here and at v 28; the ASV itself keeps them apart ('rent' / 'torn'), and 'mauled' does the same (`shavar-the-lion-mauled-1-kings-13`). *ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm hûʾ* 'It is the man of the Elohim'.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר אֶל־בָּנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר חִבְשׁוּ־לִ֖י אֶֽת־הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַֽיַּחֲבֹֽשׁוּ׃

i18n.en: And he spoke to his sons, saying, "Saddle the donkey for me." And they saddled it.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיִּמְצָ֤א אֶת־נִבְלָתוֹ֙ מֻשְׁלֶ֣כֶת בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וַֽחֲמוֹר֙ וְהָ֣אַרְיֵ֔ה עֹמְדִ֖ים אֵ֣צֶל הַנְּבֵלָ֑ה לֹֽא־אָכַ֤ל הָֽאַרְיֵה֙ אֶת־הַנְּבֵלָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁבַ֖ר אֶֽת־הַחֲמֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: And he went and found his body thrown in the way, and the donkey and the lion standing beside the body; the lion had not eaten the body nor mauled the donkey.

notes.official: *lōʾ-ʾāḵal hāʾaryēh ʾeṯ-hannəḇēlâ wəlōʾ šāḇar ʾeṯ-haḥămôr* 'the lion had not eaten the body nor mauled the donkey' (ASV 'nor torn'; `shavar-the-lion-mauled-1-kings-13`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א הַנָּבִ֜יא אֶת־נִבְלַ֧ת אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים וַיַּנִּחֵ֥הוּ אֶֽל־הַחֲמ֖וֹר וַיְשִׁיבֵ֑הוּ וַיָּבֹ֗א אֶל־עִיר֙ הַנָּבִ֣יא הַזָּקֵ֔ן לִסְפֹּ֖ד וּלְקָבְרֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the prophet took up the body of the man of the Elohim, and laid it on the donkey, and brought it back; and he came to the city of the old prophet, to mourn and to bury him.

notes.official: *lispōḏ ûləqāḇrô* 'to mourn and to bury him' (central `misped-lamentation-vocabulary-cross-corpus` cites vv 29-30; its Gen 50:10 wording is not imported). 'The body of the man of the Elohim' (*niḇlaṯ ʾîš-hāʾĕlōhîm*).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּנַּ֥ח אֶת־נִבְלָת֖וֹ בְּקִבְר֑וֹ וַיִּסְפְּד֥וּ עָלָ֖יו ה֥וֹי אָחִֽי׃

i18n.en: And he laid his body in his own grave; and they mourned over him, "Alas, my brother!"

notes.official: *hôy ʾāḥî* 'Alas, my brother!', the funeral cry (Jer 22:18). The old prophet lays the man in his own grave.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֮ אַחֲרֵ֣י קָבְר֣וֹ אֹתוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־בָּנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּמוֹתִי֙ וּקְבַרְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִ֔י בַּקֶּ֕בֶר אֲשֶׁ֛ר אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים קָב֣וּר בּ֑וֹ אֵ֚צֶל עַצְמֹתָ֔יו הַנִּ֖יחוּ אֶת־עַצְמֹתָֽי׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spoke to his sons, saying, "When I die, bury me in the grave in which the man of the Elohim is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.

notes.official: *ʾēṣel ʿaṣmōṯāyw hannîḥû ʾeṯ-ʿaṣmōṯāy* 'lay my bones beside his bones': the request is honoured when Yoshiyahu spares the bones of both men (2 Kgs 23:17-18).

paragraphs.text: כִּי֩ הָיֹ֨ה יִהְיֶ֜ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרָא֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ כָּל־בָּתֵּ֣י הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעָרֵ֥י שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃ (פ)

i18n.en: For the word which he cried by the word of YHWH against the altar in Beit-El, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Shomron, shall surely come to pass."

notes.official: *kî hāyōh yihyeh haddāḇār* 'shall surely come to pass'. *bāttê habbāmôṯ* 'the houses of the high places' (v 2). 'The cities of Shomron': Shomron (Samaria) was founded only by Omri (16:24), so the phrase uses the later name of the northern capital for its territory, a mark of the narrator's standpoint (Cogan). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) follows.

paragraphs.text: אַחַר֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לֹֽא־שָׁ֥ב יָרָבְעָ֖ם מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָרָעָ֑ה וַ֠יָּשָׁב וַיַּ֜עַשׂ מִקְצ֤וֹת הָעָם֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י בָמ֔וֹת הֶֽחָפֵץ֙ יְמַלֵּ֣א אֶת־יָד֔וֹ וִיהִ֖י כֹּהֲנֵ֥י בָמֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: After this thing Yarov'am did not turn from his evil way, but again made from among all the people priests of the high places; whoever wished, he consecrated him, that he might be one of the priests of the high places.

notes.official: *heḥāp̄ēṣ yəmallēʾ ʾeṯ-yāḏô* 'whoever wished, he consecrated him' (ASV), literally 'he filled his hand', the technical idiom of priestly installation (Ex 28:41; 29:9; Judg 17:5, 12). The ASV rendering of the idiom is kept and the literal phrase recorded here. *miqṣôṯ hāʿām* 'from among all the people' (cf. 12:31).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֙ בַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְחַטַּ֖את בֵּ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֑ם וּלְהַכְחִיד֙ וּלְהַשְׁמִ֔יד מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And by this thing it became sin to the house of Yarov'am, to cut it off and to destroy it from off the face of the ground.

notes.official: *ləḥaṭṭaʾṯ bêṯ yārāḇʿām* 'it became sin to the house of Yarov'am': the 'sin of Yarov'am' that runs through Kings to 2 Kgs 17:21-23. *mēʿal pənê hāʾăḏāmâ* 'from off the face of the ground' (central `adam-adamah`). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the chapter.
